stories.headline: Nvidia board hires Wachtell Lipton and ex-prosecutor Joon Kim to probe Huang; shares fall 5.47%

key_facts.fact: On November 10, Nvidia's independent directors retained former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run the investigation announced on Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: The probe covers whether company secrets or national security were compromised after Huang admitted an affair with a woman connected to Chinese intelligence; on Sunday the board said it had no reason to believe either was compromised.
key_facts.excerpt: hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised... Nvidia's board also said on Sunday that it has no reason to believe either national security nor Nvidia secrets were compromised.

key_facts.fact: Kim joined Wachtell only last month; in 2021 he was appointed by New York Attorney General Letitia James to investigate sexual-harassment allegations against then-Governor Andrew Cuomo.
key_facts.excerpt: Kim, a former acting attorney of the Southern District of New York, was appointed in 2021 as an independent investigator by New York Attorney General Letitia James to probe allegations of sexual harassment by former Gov. Andrew Cuomo.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has no board chair; Huang, Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have sat on the board since 1993, and the board has a combined 161 years of service.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia board has a combined 161 years of service... Huang, Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have sat on it since 1993, according to Nvidia's proxy statement. Nvidia has a lead independent director instead of a board chair.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell 5.47% on Tuesday, November 10, after a drop of more than 4% on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia shares sank 5.47% on Tuesday as investors continued to weigh the potential fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia closed at $168.89; Korean chipmakers still rallied the next day, with SK hynix up 5.4% and Samsung Electronics up 3.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia fell to $168.89 overnight after its independent directors opened an investigation... SK hynix rose 5.4 percent to 1,277,000 won ($957.0). Samsung Electronics gained a smaller 3.6 percent to 206,000 won

stories.headline: FT: Commerce stalls Megaspeed blacklisting over four agencies' objections; scandal boosts NDAA chip curbs

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported on November 10 that the Pentagon and the State, Energy and Treasury departments pushed to add Singapore-based Megaspeed to the Entity List, but Commerce has delayed new additions for two months.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. Department of Commerce put on hold a proposal to add Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed to the Entity List... despite major departments, including the Departments of Defense, State and the Treasury, calling for Megaspeed to be added... delayed the process of designating new entities for sanctions over the past two months

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment with Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, and Commerce has not added any company to the Entity List in more than a year, its longest gap in 18 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Speedmatrix reportedly 'purchased at least $4.8 billion worth of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026,' per the FT... 'has not added a company to the entity list in more than a year, the longest stretch without such a listing in 18 years,'

key_facts.fact: Commerce said it needs more information on some companies, and Nvidia said it put Megaspeed on its internal block list in June 2025 and halted sales and shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce officials told other agencies they needed additional information on some companies... 'we placed the company on our internal block list in June 2025 and halted additional sales and shipments.'

key_facts.fact: Politico reported that lawmakers, aides and lobbyists say the scandal has significantly raised the chances that Congress enacts chip export limits this year in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), and that Nvidia is now leaning on tech allies and customers to argue its case.
key_facts.excerpt: the revelation that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy has significantly raised the chances that Congress will enact chip export limits this year as part of a must-pass defense package, known as the National Defense Authorization Act... Nvidia appears to have shifted its strategy to lean on tech sector allies and major customers

key_facts.fact: Republican Rep. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren urged action on chip export controls, and a floor vote on the NDAA is seen as possible in the second week of December.
key_facts.excerpt: Republican Rep. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren issued a bipartisan statement urging immediate action on export controls for AI semiconductors bound for China... with a floor vote in the second week of December

stories.headline: Reuters: PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on November 11 that Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two Nvidia H200 chips for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), per an October 21 procurement record on its website.
key_facts.excerpt: Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website.

key_facts.fact: The university is one of China's 'Seven Sons of National Defense' and has been on the Entity List since 2001; it bought the chips from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology, not Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Northwestern is a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense"... The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia... added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001

key_facts.fact: Its cybersecurity school also signed two seven-month contracts in January for access to servers with eight H200s each (441,700 and 441,000 yuan), and rented servers with A100 and A800 chips, which are banned for all Chinese entities.
key_facts.excerpt: Northwestern Polytechnical also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies

key_facts.fact: A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting Nvidia-powered computing through domestic suppliers.
key_facts.excerpt: A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers.

key_facts.fact: Trump's case-by-case H200 export licensing, which began in January, did not lift the separate restrictions on Entity List organisations.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump's administration began allowing some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis in January. But that policy did not lift the separate restrictions applying to Entity List organisations

stories.headline: AMD ships 6th Gen EPYC 'Venice' server CPUs on Zen 6, with up to 256 cores

key_facts.fact: On November 10, AMD announced general availability of its 6th Gen EPYC SP7 server processors (codename Venice) on the Zen 6 architecture, with systems shipping from all leading server vendors.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced the general availability of the 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ server SP7 processors, based on the new "Zen 6" architecture... Systems powered by the new CPUs are shipping from all leading server vendors

key_facts.fact: The chips offer up to 256 cores and 512 threads, clocks up to 5.3 GHz with 96 cores, up to 1.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth per socket and PCIe Gen 6.
key_facts.excerpt: up to 256 cores and 512 threads... Frequencies up to 5.3 GHz with 96 cores... up to 1.6 TB/s of memory bandwidth per socket... PCIe® Gen 6 I/O for x86 platforms

key_facts.fact: AMD claims 1.9x the throughput of the prior 'Turin' generation and, for its 256-core 400-watt part, 3.3 times the AI agents per watt of Nvidia's Vera CPU.
key_facts.excerpt: the Venice chips delivering 1.9X the throughput of the prior "Turin" Epyc 9005 processors... AMD's 6th Gen 256-core chip at 400 watts offers 3.3 times the agents-per-watt that Nvidia's Vera does

key_facts.fact: Meta is a lead customer validating the platform, Microsoft Azure has HDv2 instances in preview, and Oracle's OCI Compute E7 instances will use the chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is working with AMD as a lead customer... Azure HDv2 now in preview... OCI Compute E7 cloud compute instances will be powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC server processors

key_facts.fact: Tom's Hardware's benchmarks found the chips use TSMC's N2P process, the 9686F often beats Nvidia's Vera, and a dual EPYC 9996 is up to 93% faster than a dual Zen 5 EPYC 9965.
key_facts.excerpt: uses TSMC's N2P, the 9686F often beats Nvidia's Vera, a dual 9996 is up to 93% faster than a dual Zen 5 9965

key_facts.fact: TDPs rise to as much as 600 watts on SP7, and the EPYC 9006X and lower-power Verano variants are still months away.
key_facts.excerpt: EPYC 9006X And Verano Not Coming For Months - TDPs Increased Up To 600W... TDPs for SP7 CPUs will scale from 400 watts up to 600 watts

stories.headline: CoreWeave Q3 revenue jumps 168% to $3.66B, backlog hits $132.5B and guidance rises

key_facts.fact: On November 10, CoreWeave reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3.661 billion, up from $1.365 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of $709 million against $110 million a year earlier.
Revenue backlog reached about $132.5 billion on September 30, up from $104 billion in June; revenue beat the $3.55 billion analyst estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue: $3.66 billion vs. $3.55 billion expected... the company now sitting on a $132.5 billion revenue backlog, up from $104 billion as of June.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-13.3 billion, adjusted operating income guidance to $1.275-1.375 billion and 2026 capex to $37-39 billion, and expects more than 1.85 GW of active power at year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: We are raising our full year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion... We continue to expect more than 1.85 gigawatts of active power at year-end. We now expect full year 2026 capital expenditures of $37 billion to $39 billion

key_facts.fact: CEO Michael Intrator said the company expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months.
key_facts.excerpt: approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months alone

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave carried about $46.9 billion of recourse and non-recourse debt at September 30, and guides Q4 interest expense at $1.05-1.15 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Recourse and non-recourse debt totaled about $46.9 billion at Sept. 30, while fourth-quarter interest expense is guided to $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion.

stories.headline: SpaceX signs Singulus deal for solar-cell lines to power Starmind orbital compute satellites

key_facts.fact: On November 10, Singulus Technologies announced a supply contract with SpaceX for a turnkey heterojunction (HJT) solar-cell production line, the first of several planned lines.
key_facts.excerpt: today announced it has signed a supply contract with SpaceX for a turnkey production line for the manufacture of heterojunction solar cells. This supply contract is part of a strategic partnership with SpaceX under which SINGULUS is planning to deliver multiple additional lines.

key_facts.fact: The first line will be delivered in the first half of 2027, and production will scale to support more than 100 GW of production equipment at SpaceX's Bastrop, Texas, satellite factory.
key_facts.excerpt: The first production line will be delivered in the first half of 2027, and production will scale to support more than 100 GW of production equipment as SpaceX accelerates satellite manufacturing in Bastrop, Texas.

key_facts.fact: Musk wrote that SpaceX had ordered 100 GW per year of HJT solar manufacturing equipment from Singulus 'for Starmind to create a sentient sun.'
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX has ordered 100 GW/year of HJT solar manufacturing equipment from Singulus in Germany. This is for Starmind to create a sentient sun.

key_facts.fact: The first line is worth more than €60 million ($67 million), and Starmind satellites are meant to run AI computing payloads on solar power in orbit; SpaceX specs for its AI1 satellite list a payload drawing 175 kW on average.
key_facts.excerpt: SINGULUS's first production line for SpaceX is worth more than €60 million... The cells are intended for SpaceX's Starmind satellites, which are designed to run computing payloads using solar power generated in orbit... a computing payload drawing up to 250 kilowatts at peak and 175 kilowatts on average.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX funded Singulus in March 2026 and again in October 2026 through a subordinated secured loan.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX provided significant funding to SINGULUS in March 2026 and additionally in October 2026 as part of the recently announced subordinated secured loan.

stories.headline: WSJ: SoftBank reserved more than 13 GW of gas turbines for AI before taking a $3.7B loss

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported that SoftBank had reserved gas turbines totaling well over 13 GW, more than six Hoover Dams, mostly from GE Vernova, which is more than even the world's largest gas plant could use.
key_facts.excerpt: At its peak, SoftBank had locked in more than 13 gigawatts worth of turbine capacity, enough to match the output of over six Hoover Dams combined... Most of the hardware was reserved from GE Vernova

key_facts.fact: SoftBank booked a $3.7 billion (¥597.2 billion) loss on revised power-equipment procurement for US AI data centers: $2.9 billion on non-refundable advance payments and $0.9 billion on contract modifications and settlements.
key_facts.excerpt: (1) Loss on non-refundable advance payments $2.9B (¥457.0B)... Total loss $3.7B (¥597.2B)... (2) Loss on contract modifications and settlements $0.9B (¥140.2B)

key_facts.fact: Cumulative payments for the equipment reached $9.5 billion, of which $6.6 billion goes to the PORTS-Pike power project in Ohio and others; SoftBank may get up to $2.1 billion in rebates on future purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: Cumulative payments from FY2025 through Q2 FY2026: $9.5B... $6.6B allocated to power generation-related equipment purchases for PORTS-Pike power generation project and others... Rights to receive rebates of up to $2.1B

key_facts.fact: CFO Yoshimitsu Goto rejected Elon Musk's November 6 claim that SoftBank had 'defaulted' on its turbine orders.
key_facts.excerpt: SBG Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Yoshimitsu Goto denied Musk's default claim at an earnings briefing the previous day... Goto said he had "no idea at all why [Musk] posted that,"

key_facts.fact: SoftBank swung to a fiscal Q2 net loss of ¥1.12 trillion ($7 billion), hit by the turbine write-down and a fall in its Intel stake.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank reported a fiscal second-quarter net loss of 1.12 trillion yen ($7 billion) on Tuesday, as losses tied to U.S. AI data center equipment procurement and Intel share declines weighed on earnings.
